blocks.text: Fixed asset and lease accounting policy
HANGS Construction Services LLC
Status: approved by the board, effective July 1, 2025
1. What is capitalized
1.1 Equipment with a cost of $5,000.00 or more and a life of more than one year is capitalized at its full cost: price, delivery, assembly and setup.
1.2 Repairs and maintenance, including rebuilds of an existing asset’s parts that keep it working, are expensed when incurred.
1.3 Every purchase of $25,000.00 or more needs a capital expenditure request approved by the president before the order is placed.
2. Depreciation
2.1 Straight-line by month on cost less salvage, rounded to the cent, a full month in the month placed in service and none in the month of disposal; the last month takes what is left.
2.2 Lives and salvage by class (used equipment takes its class life unless the equipment manager documents a shorter one):
Class: Heavy earthmoving equipment; life 120 months; salvage 20% of cost
Class: Cranes and crane attachments; life 240 months; salvage 20% of cost
Class: Concrete pump trucks; life 120 months; salvage 15% of cost
Class: Trucks and trailers; life 96 months; salvage 15% of cost
Class: Site office units; life 180 months; salvage 0% of cost
Class: Loaders, telehandlers and skid steers; life 84 months; salvage 10% of cost
Class: Survey and layout equipment; life 60 months; salvage 0% of cost
2.3 A disposal removes the asset’s cost and accumulated depreciation; the difference from the proceeds is a gain or loss in equipment costs.
3. Leases
3.1 Every agreement for equipment or space is read under ASC 842: a lease is a contract for the right to control an identified asset for a period.
3.2 Leases of 12 months or less with no purchase option HGC is reasonably certain to exercise are short-term: expensed, not recognized.
3.3 Other leases are recognized at the present value of the payments, discounted at the incremental borrowing rate, the equipment term loan’s 7.10%.
Demonstration document. Every name and figure is invented.
